nodes.description: The vulnerable RLE sanity check evaluates `_starttab[o]` for all `_numrows` rows even though EOF left most of `_starttab` uninitialized. In the crashing case it checks 32 rows after only 1 row was initialized.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable debugger checkpoint at the sanity-check site shows `_numrows = 32` while the `_starttab` shadow has only its first 4-byte element unpoisoned.

edges.description: The partially initialized `_starttab` state created when the EOF-bounded fill loop exits persists unchanged to the later sanity check because the vulnerable original performs no intervening write that defines the unread tail entries.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable debugger checkpoints at lines 335 and 352 observe the same `_starttab` pointer and the same shadow layout: 1 initialized row followed by poisoned tail rows.

root_cause_criterion.obligation: All `_numrows` `_starttab` entries are initialized before the RLE sanity check executes.
root_cause_criterion.description: After the EOF-bounded `_starttab` fill loop stops, the parser must define every unread `_starttab` element before the later sanity-check loop consumes all `_numrows` entries. The fixed binary satisfies this by zero-filling the unread tail before the sanity check executes.
root_cause_criterion.evidence: At the vulnerable post-loop checkpoint `_numrows = 32` but only 1 `_starttab` row is initialized; at the fixed post-fill checkpoint all 32 rows are initialized and the sanity-check path still executes.
